findings.problem: A failed verification returning after timeout reopened an unknown card to pending, retaining the old outcomeId.
findings.before: The regression observed pending with sendError after the unknown outcome committed.
findings.fix: Reopen rechecks the current sending state and absence of a terminal outcome under the existing locks.

findings.problem: Successful verification after timeout could start the external operation even though the card was already terminal.
findings.before: The regression observed one synthetic transport entry after the unknown outcome committed.
findings.fix: After verification and attachment preparation, serialize the dispatch decision against card mutation and recheck state, outcome and attempt identity. No lock is held across connector execution.
findings.boundary: A terminal outcome committed before dispatch is claimed prevents dispatch. An operation already claimed or entered before timeout remains potentially in flight; unknown is not a cancellation or remote-send recall.

findings.problem: Refresh read an old sending state, paused during invocation lookup and then settled a reopened card or a later attempt.
findings.before: The regression turned a pending card into unknown; a timestamp-only intermediate fix also failed when the next attempt had the same timestamp.
findings.fix: Settlement rechecks sending state plus attempt identity under the mutation lock. New sends carry a private random sendAttemptId; legacy sending receipts remain recoverable with the existing timestamp fallback.
